instructions: At least 1 hour before dinner, or that morning, tip the 1 lb crab meat onto a plate and pick through it with your fingers for any hard bits of shell or cartilage. Try to keep the lumps whole.
In a large bowl, whisk 1/4 cup mayonnaise, the egg, 1 tbsp Dijon, 1 tbsp Worcestershire and the 1 tsp Old Bay until smooth.

Finely chop 1 1/2 tbsp of the parsley. Zest 1 tsp from the lemon. Add both to the bowl with the crab, the 1/2 cup panko, 1/4 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper. Fold it together gently with a spatula until the crumbs are mixed in. Stop there so the crab stays in chunks.

Scoop the mixture into 8 cakes of about 1/3 cup each and press each one lightly into a patty about 1 inch thick. Set them on a plate, cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour. Chilled cakes hold together in the pan.

While they chill, make the tartar sauce. Stir 1/2 cup mayonnaise with the 1 tbsp relish, 1/2 tsp Dijon and 2 tsp juice from the zested lemon. Cover and refrigerate it. Cut the rest of the lemon into wedges.
When you're ready to cook, heat the 1/4 cup canola oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium until it shimmers. Lay in the crab cakes with space between them. Stand back a little. They'll spatter.

Cook them for 3 to 4 minutes without moving them, until the underside is deep golden. Flip them gently with a thin spatula and cook the other side for 3 to 4 minutes, until it's golden too and the cakes are hot all the way through.
Move them to a plate lined with paper towels for a minute. Taste a corner of one. If it's flat, sprinkle a pinch more salt over the hot cakes, or add a squeeze of the lemon.
Serve with the tartar sauce and the lemon wedges.
advance_prep_notes: Shape the crab cakes and chill them at least 1 hour ahead (that morning is fine).
method_notes: Both read versions bind 1 lb lump crab with very little: an egg, mayo, Dijon, Worcestershire, Old Bay and 1/2 cup panko, folded gently so the lumps stay whole, then chill the shaped cakes at least an hour and pan-fry them in oil in a nonstick pan over medium, 3 to 5 minutes a side. Spend With Pennies adds parsley, lemon zest and pepper and makes 6 to 8 cakes; Once Upon a Chef adds diced celery, uses two eggs, makes 6 larger cakes and serves them with a quick tartar sauce of mayo, relish, Dijon, red onion and lemon. This follows Spend With Pennies (its kosher salt cut to 1/4 tsp table salt) and borrows Once Upon a Chef's tartar sauce without the onion.
